description: We are a team of innovators exploring how technology, space biology, and data-driven insights can support astronaut health during long-duration space missions. Through ASTRA Human Health Beyond Earth, we aim to develop an interactive health-monitoring platform that helps visualize health indicators, explore changes over time, connect observations with scientific research, and support informed health assessment.
summary:
ASTRA PULSE is a web-based astronaut health monitoring and crew-support platform designed around the challenges of long-duration human spaceflight. It brings health information, mission context, educational explanations, research resources, and care-support guidance together in one accessible interface.

The platform organizes important health topics—including cardiovascular function, sleep, nutrition, immune health, behavioral well-being, and spaceflight environmental risks—into dedicated sections. Its features include a health overview, health readings, an interactive body explorer, health intelligence, trend analysis, mission information, care guidance, daily tasks, medical support information, and a research library.

ASTRA PULSE draws on publicly available NASA and space-agency research to help make complex space-health information easier to understand and navigate. Its goal is to support health awareness, encourage consistent monitoring, and help crew members recognize when communication with authorized medical personnel may be appropriate.

The project supports safer, better-informed human exploration by putting crew health information at the center of mission operations.
details:
ASTRA PULSE is a responsive web application developed to help astronauts understand and organize health information during long-duration space missions.

The platform is structured around a central overview and a set of connected sections: Health Readings, Body Explorer, Health Intelligence, Trend Analysis, Mission Center, Care Guidance, Research Library, My Health Profile, Daily Tasks, Medical Support, and About ASTRA PULSE.

Users can navigate health topics, explore the relationship between human physiology and spaceflight conditions, review health information, and access research resources. The platform is designed to make complex information easier to understand through visual organization, explanatory content, and a consistent interface.

The project considers the major challenges of human spaceflight, including radiation exposure, altered gravity, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, and the demands of closed environments. It draws on public research and resources from NASA and other space-agency sources.

ASTRA PULSE was developed as a web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Its design includes responsive navigation, dashboard components, visual elements, interactive page features, and research links.

The intended impact is to improve health awareness and make relevant information easier for crew members to access during missions. The platform is a prototype and is not connected to live spacecraft sensors or clinical records. It does not diagnose conditions or replace professional medical judgment. Any future operational use would require validation, secure data integration, and approval by authorized flight medical teams.
